segments.text: Proposition 47. In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.
Let the square on BA be described, and likewise the squares on AC and BC.
I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA and AC.
For parallelograms on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another.
Therefore the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the sum of the two squares on the sides containing the right angle.
